A write-ahead log, or WAL, is a component of a database that records all changes made to the database. When a transaction is initiated, the database starts writing the changes to the log before it actually makes the changes to the database itself. This ensures that all changes are safely recorded before the database is updated. If a crash occurs before the database is updated, the database can use the log to recover the changes that were made since the last checkpoint (at which point the changes were written from the log to the database). The database can then replay the changes from the log, restoring the database to a consistent state.
In the event of a crash, the database can recover from the last checkpoint, and the changes in the log will be replayed to bring the database back up to date. This approach ensures that the database is always in a consistent state, even after a crash. If the database crashes before the changes are written to the log, the changes will be discarded and the database will be left in a consistent state.
